Kenya_2026-04-20_weekly_precip_downscale: Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 20 to 27 April exceeds 80 mm in the west between Lake Victoria and the western highlands, in the central highlands near the equator and locally on the north coast, with the north-central interior below 10 mm. The week of 27 April to 4 May is by far the wettest, with 60 to 98 mm across the west, several maxima above 90 mm in the north-centre between 2N and 4N, the central highlands, the north coast and near the southern border, and only the eastern interior below 20 mm. From 4 May the rain contracts to the west, the central highlands and a 70 to 98 mm strip along the south coast, and by 25 May to 1 June most of the country is below 20 mm.
Kenya_2026-04-20_anomaly_from_50th: The ensemble mean for 20 to 27 April is 15 to 30 mm below the model-climate median in the west and southwest between the equator and 2S, and 30 to 40 mm above it on the south coast. For 27 April to 4 May the anomaly turns positive over most of the west and centre (+20 to +35 mm), reaching +40 to +55 mm over Lake Victoria at the western edge of the domain. From 4 May to 1 June anomalies stay within about 10 mm of the median, apart from a persistent deficit of 15 to 25 mm in the cell on the Lake Victoria shore at the equator.
Kenya_2026-03-20_weekly_precip: ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 20 to 27 March is widespread at 40 to 60 mm, with 70 to 80 mm in the west near 2N and in the southwest near 3S, more than 100 mm over Lake Victoria and 80 to 100 mm on the south coast, while the northeast along the Somali border stays below 25 mm. Totals drop sharply from 27 March, to 20 to 40 mm over most areas and less than 15 mm in the north-centre between 2N and 4N. From 3 April to 1 May the southwest and south-centre hold 30 to 50 mm per week and the north and east 15 to 30 mm.
Kenya_2026-03-20_anomaly_from_50th: The ensemble mean for 20 to 27 March is above the model-climate median everywhere, by 20 to 45 mm over most of Kenya, 50 to 60 mm in the west near the Uganda border and on the south coast, and up to about 85 mm over Lake Victoria at the western edge of the domain. For 27 March to 3 April the surplus falls to 5 to 20 mm and the southwest across the Tanzanian border turns slightly negative (-5 to -10 mm). Weak positive anomalies of 5 to 20 mm persist from 3 April to 1 May, with a small deficit on the Lake Victoria shore at the equator.
Kenya_2026-01-15_weekly_precip: Kenya is virtually dry in the ECMWF S2S ensemble mean from 15 to 29 January (below 2 mm), with only 10 to 20 mm at the far southwestern edge of the domain over Lake Victoria and northern Tanzania. Rain builds in the southwest from 29 January, reaching 30 to 50 mm at the western edge and 15 to 20 mm in southwest Kenya in the week of 5 to 12 February. From 12 to 26 February the southwest near the Tanzanian border receives 20 to 35 mm and the central highlands 10 to 15 mm, while the north and east stay below 5 mm throughout.
Kenya_2026-01-15_anomaly_from_50th: The ensemble mean for 15 to 29 January is 10 to 20 mm below the model-climate median in the southwest along the Tanzanian border, with deficits of 25 to 38 mm further south in northern Tanzania, and close to the median in the north. The deficits fade in the week of 29 January to 5 February. From 5 to 26 February the anomaly turns positive, at +10 to +20 mm over southwest Kenya, +8 to +12 mm in the central highlands and +25 to +38 mm over Lake Victoria at the western edge of the domain.
